Crypto.com is a global cryptocurrency platform serving traders and investors in markets around the world. The CDC product line is our international crypto trading app — spanning spot, perpetual contracts, and card rips — and we are building the next generation of trading products for a global audience.

We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Growth to sit at the intersection of user acquisition, creative strategy, martech, and measurement. This is not a single-lane role. You’ll own the day-to-day performance of our UA program across paid channels and every market we operate in, but you’ll also lead three critical sub-functions — creative, martech, and measurement — that today sit with senior leadership and need a dedicated operator to take them to the next level.

You’ll work directly with our agency partners, product teams, data science, and platform reps (Meta, Google, Apple) across regions. You’ll inherit a scaled UA program with multiple products launching simultaneously, a global market footprint, and a martech stack that’s being built in real time. If you’re the kind of person who can context-switch between a Meta CAPI payload spec and a creative brief in the same afternoon, this role was made for you.

Responsibilities 
User Acquisition Operations

• Own the weekly operating rhythm for CDC paid UA — spend plans, pacing, optimization decisions, and performance reporting across all channels (Meta, Google, Apple Search, programmatic DSPs, affiliates, regional platforms, and emerging networks), across every market we operate in

• Manage the relationship with our performance agency on a daily basis — standups, creative briefings, channel strategy, spend allocation, and trading decisions

• Drive channel-level optimization using CAC, CPFT, pLTV ROAS, and lower-funnel conversion metrics. You’re expected to know what’s working, what’s not, and why before anyone asks

• Lead GTM execution for new product launches and market openings (spot, perpetual contracts, card rips, new offer structures) — from tracking readiness through creative production through spend activation

• Build and maintain the weekly trading deck and leadership updates. Present performance narratives to VP and C-level stakeholders with clarity and confidence

• Own the competitive monitoring cadence — Sensor Tower, app store rankings, ad intelligence — across key markets, and translate competitive signals into channel and creative decisions

• Own market prioritisation — which countries we open, in what order, and what each market needs in localisation, payment rails, and channel mix before we commit spend

Sub-function: Creative Strategy

Our creative pipeline is currently managed between agency and leadership. This role takes ownership of the full creative lifecycle for performance marketing.

• Own the creative learning agenda — what hooks, formats, and concepts we’re testing, what’s winning, and what to kill. Maintain a structured view of creative performance by channel, format, and audience

• Lead creative briefing for the agency and UGC creators. Translate product updates, offers, and cultural moments into production-ready briefs with clear deliverables and timelines, localised for each market we run in

• Drive format expansion beyond static display — UGC video, social-native content, meme-format creative, and AI-assisted production pipelines

• Establish a rapid refresh cadence to combat creative fatigue across channels, and ensure channel-specific sizing and placement specs are met

• Coordinate with brand and content teams on production shoots, scripting, and asset capture for UA use

Sub-function: Martech

Our martech stack spans AppsFlyer, Segment, Firebase, Google Tag Manager, Meta CAPI, Impact (affiliates), and multiple ad platform integrations. Today this is led by our VP with execution support from a solo martech lead. This role becomes the strategic owner.

• Serve as the growth team’s primary point of contact for all tracking, attribution, and signal infrastructure. You’re the person who knows whether events are firing, payloads are complete, and platform signals are flowing

• Partner with our martech lead to prioritize and unblock implementation work — new product event instrumentation, platform pixel/CAPI builds, conversion upload pipelines, and deep link configuration

• Own the relationship with platform measurement teams (Google gTech, Meta measurement partners, AppsFlyer TAMs) across regions and ensure their recommendations translate into shipped work

• Drive martech readiness for every product launch and offer change. If tracking isn’t ready, you’re the one who flags it and owns the escalation

• Understand the full signal chain from user action to ad platform optimization loop — SDK events, server-to-server integrations, CAPI payloads, consent parameters, and AEM eligibility requirements

• Handle the multi-market layer — regional MMP configuration, multi-currency revenue handling, and market-specific consent and privacy regimes

Sub-function: Measurement

Measurement maturity is the constraint on scaling. This role owns the roadmap for closing attribution gaps and building toward incrementality-based decision-making.

• Own the attribution framework — last-click, MECE logic, promo code overlap rules — and ensure it’s consistently applied across reporting, agency data, and leadership updates

• Define and maintain measurement plans for each product line (spot, perps, rips) including KPI definitions, LTV attribution windows, and what “success” looks like at each funnel stage

• Lead the build-out of conversion feedback loops for each platform — Google Ads click ID upload pipelines, Meta CAPI integration, and Apple SKAN/AdAttributionKit readiness

• Partner with data science on pLTV model validation, cohort economics tracking, and the eventual transition from CPA to ROAS-based bidding

• Scope and prioritize incrementality testing (geo holdouts, per-channel lift measurement) and marketing mix modeling as the program matures

• Maintain reporting credibility — when agency data and Tableau data don’t match, you’re the person who investigates, explains, and fixes it

• Normalise reporting across currencies and markets so performance is comparable country to country, and so a CAC in one region means the same thing as a CAC in another

Requirements: 
• 5+ years in performance marketing or growth, with direct ownership of paid UA budgets across Meta, Google, Apple Search, and at least one programmatic partner

• Hands-on experience with mobile measurement partners (AppsFlyer, Adjust, or Branch), server-to-server integrations, and ad platform conversion APIs (Meta CAPI, Google Ads S2S)

• Experience marketing trading or investing products — you understand funding rates, spreads, deposit and withdrawal flows, and why an active trader’s value profile looks different from a casual user’s

• Track record running paid UA across multiple international markets — localisation, regional channel mix, a multi-time-zone operating rhythm, and market-by-market regulatory nuance

• Strong working knowledge of attribution models, SKAN/AdAttributionKit, AEM eligibility, and the privacy-era signal landscape

• Experience managing or closely partnering with a performance creative function — you’ve briefed UGC creators, reviewed ad concepts, and made data-backed creative decisions

• Comfort with ambiguity and competing priorities. You’ll be launching multiple products, fixing attribution gaps, and building new measurement infrastructure simultaneously

• Exceptional communication skills — you can explain a CAPI payload issue to an engineer and a CAC trend to a CMO in the same day

• Experience in crypto, trading, fintech, or financial services is strongly preferred — you’ve marketed a product where the user is putting capital at risk. What matters most is that you’ve scaled paid UA in a high-velocity, multi-product environment

Why This Role: 
• You’re joining at an inflection point — new products launching, measurement stack being built, creative pipeline evolving. The person in this seat will shape how all of it comes together

• You’ll have real ownership across UA, creative, martech, and measurement. This is not a channel manager role — it’s a multi-discipline growth operator role with a clear path to director

• You’ll work with a small, senior team that moves fast and makes real decisions. No layers of approval — the VP is your skip and the CMO is one level above that

• Part of Crypto.com — a global platform with the resources and ambition to build a category-defining product, and the speed and autonomy of a startup growth team

• Global remit — the markets you open and the playbooks you build will define how we scale internationally, not just in one country

Who We Are: NEXT Ventures / FundedNext
NEXT Ventures Ltd. is a global fintech group that owns and operates FundedNext, a leading proprietary trading platform, and FNmarkets, a CFD brokerage. Operating across five countries, the group brings together a diverse team of professionals to deliver technology-driven trading solutions and serve a global community of traders from over 170 countries.

Your Role in Our Mission
As an IC2 – Sr Executive, FP&A, you sit at the intersection of finance, ERP architecture, and data engineering. You will play a hands-on role in our Oracle NetSuite and Oracle EPM Cloud implementations—owning historical data migrations, building automated API and SQL pipelines, deploying validated AI-assisted finance workflows, and delivering high-precision management and cash-position reporting across the group.

How You’ll Make an Impact (Key Responsibilities)
1. Oracle NetSuite — Configuration Support & Data Operations
•
System Configuration: Execute NetSuite configuration tasks assigned by the FP&A Head and Manager during the ongoing implementation.
•
Group Data Migration: Own historical transaction imports and reconcile migrated data against QuickBooks, Xero, and bank statements with reconciliation-evidenced accuracy of at least 99% before each cutover phase.
•
UAT & Cutover Readiness: Participate in UAT cycles for group and subsidiary workflows; document defects, retest fixes, and prepare evidence packs for stakeholder sign-off per phase.
•
Reporting & Dashboards: Build and maintain saved searches, custom reports, and SuiteAnalytics dashboards covering subsidiary and group P&L, cost-centre performance, and cash position.
•
First-Line Support: Act as the first point of contact for NetSuite queries from finance wings, escalating system issues to the Manager with full documentation.
2. Data Engineering, Integration & APIs
•
Automated Pipelines: Design and maintain automated data pipelines between NetSuite, Oracle EPM Cloud, PSP settlement reports, bank statements, and Google Sheets using SuiteTalk REST APIs, CSV automation, and scripting (Python / Apps Script).
•
SQL Extracts: Build and maintain SQL-based extracts for ad hoc reporting, reconciliation, and cross-entity intercompany matching.
•
AI-Assisted Finance Workflows: Develop AI-assisted workflows (Claude/Copilot-class tooling, prompt-driven validation, agent/MCP integrations) for reconciliation checks, variance commentary drafts, and data-quality flagging—adopted after FP&A Manager validation of outputs.
•
Workflow Automation: Implement SuiteFlow and workflow automation to eliminate documented manual steps, maintaining a before/after log of hours saved per automation.
3. Oracle EPM Cloud — Implementation Support & Data Operations
•
EPM Integrations & Scripting: Support EPM Cloud implementation by building and testing Data Management integrations from NetSuite (P&L, Balance Sheet, cash flow actuals), maintaining dimension/metadata mappings, and scripting recurring loads via EPM Automate.
•
Actuals Monitoring: Monitor actuals-feed completeness as the source for group consolidation, flagging discrepancies within 24 hours with documented root causes.
•
Budgeting & Forecasting: Support annual budgeting and rolling forecast cycles by coordinating input collection from department heads, cleaning submissions, and uploading into EPM templates.
•
Output Validation: Validate EPM report outputs (Balance Sheet, P&L, SBU, cost-centre) against NetSuite actuals and recommend them to the FP&A Manager for sign-off.
4. Financial Reporting & Analysis
•
Monthly Management Reporting: Prepare monthly management reports (P&L, Balance Sheet, cash flow) with variance analysis against budget and prior period; deliver within the group close calendar (WD5 currently; T+3 target post-ERP stabilisation) with reconciliation-evidenced accuracy of at least 98%.
•
Weekly Flash Reporting: Produce the weekly flash report consolidating cash balances, inflows, outflows, and net position across all PSP and bank accounts, delivered by T+1.
5. Data Quality, Documentation & Collaboration
•
SOP Maintenance: Maintain current SOPs for all owned data migration tasks, pipelines, reporting workflows, and NetSuite processes in ClickUp per FP&A wing standards.
•
Data Governance: Partner with all finance wings on data governance, internal controls, and access management for NetSuite financial records.
•
Stakeholder Alignment: Keep the FP&A Head and Manager updated on implementation progress, data-quality issues, and deliverable status via Jira and Slack.

What You Bring (Required Qualifications & Skills)
•
Educational Background: Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field—or a Finance/Accounting degree backed by a demonstrated technical portfolio (SQL projects, automation builds, API integrations).
•
FP&A & ERP Experience: 3+ years of hands-on FP&A or financial reporting experience with direct involvement in an ERP implementation or migration (Oracle NetSuite preferred).
•
Database & SQL Mastery: Strong SQL skills for financial data extraction and validation, with experience querying relational databases in a finance or reporting context.
•
Automation & Integration: Demonstrated experience building REST APIs, Python or Apps Script automations, and CSV/ETL pipelines, with the ability to walk through at least one end-to-end build.
•
Practical AI Tooling: Hands-on experience deploying AI-assisted finance workflows (LLM tooling for data validation, reconciliation, or reporting) rather than surface-level familiarity.
•
NetSuite Proficiency: Working knowledge of NetSuite (Chart of Accounts, saved searches, SuiteAnalytics, CSV imports); SuiteScript exposure is a strong plus.
•
EPM Exposure: Familiarity with Oracle EPM Cloud (Planning/Budgeting, Data Management, EPM Automate) is advantageous.
•
Requirements Translation: Ability to gather, document, and translate business requirements into system configurations or reporting specifications.

You will determine how they apply to OKX’s activities and help build a reliable process for meeting each obligation.

Most of the work is data and judgment: deciding what is reportable, by which entity, and to whom, then making sure the right trade and lifecycle data reaches the right swap data repository, trade repository, or regulator on time and reconciles to our trading records. You will own reporting scoping/eligibility, submission monitoring, and the controls that show our reports are complete, accurate, and timely.

You will work with Trading, Product, Engineering, Data, Legal, local Compliance teams and reporting providers, and you will lead regulatory change in this space. Responsibilities for source data, systems, submissions and remediation will be agreed across those teams; you will lead the compliance framework and stay close enough to the process to identify and proactively resolve problems. You will report to the Head of Markets and Product Compliance and support a central function that owns reporting interpretation, scoping, oversight, and remediation for every entity in scope.

•

Interpret and apply derivatives and transaction reporting rules across global regimes, including CFTC Part 45, MiFIR Article 26, EMIR Article 9, UK MiFIR, UK EMIR, and the ASIC Derivative Transaction Rules (Reporting) 2024, exercising independent technical judgment, supported by Legal and outside counsel.

•

Own and maintain entity, product, and transaction-level reporting scoping and eligibility: which entity reports, which products and lifecycle events are in scope, which counterparty role triggers the obligation, and which repository or authority receives the report.

•

Oversee, support, and help maintain the daily reporting process. Monitor submissions against deadlines, including T+1 for MiFIR transaction reports, investigate rejections and breaks, and track each one to resolution.

•

Reconcile reported activity to trading records and repository data, and coordinate corrections and back-reporting with the teams that own the relevant systems and data.

•

Define and maintain the reporting data specification with Engineering and Data, including field-level mapping, reference data such as LEIs, UTIs, UPIs, and ISINs, and the validation rules applied before submission.

Build and run the control framework: completeness, accuracy, and timeliness checks, exception management, management information, and records that hold up to regulator and audit review.

Drive reporting readiness and remediation. Assess new derivatives products, new entities, and regulatory changes, identify control gaps, agree on owners and deadlines across Compliance, Operations, Product, and Engineering, and track delivery.

Escalate material issues. Assess the impact of reporting errors, escalate to senior management, and support notifications to regulators where required.

As an Information Security Risk Manager, you will play a key role in shaping a structured, data-driven approach to information security risk management at Exness, helping the business make better decisions through quantitative risk analysis.

Every year, Exness makes dozens of high-value security and technology decisions involving millions of dollars — from security investments and vendor selection to architecture changes, cyber insurance, and release readiness.

Your focus will be on quantifying uncertainty to support these decisions, moving beyond traditional risk registers, 5x5 risk matrices, and heat maps towards evidence-based financial risk modelling.

We are looking for someone who can demonstrate the financial impact of different options. For example: "Option A reduces our 1-in-20-year loss from $8M to $3M for $400K. Option B costs half as much but leaves the tail almost unchanged."

The ideal candidate is an experienced, hands-on risk management professional with strong analytical capabilities, able to work independently, influence stakeholders, and translate complex risk scenarios into actionable business insights.

The role is based in our Limassol office, Cyprus. In case of relocation, we offer full relocation support for you and your family to make your move smooth and worry-free.

What you'll actually do

• Support specific decisions. Build quantitative models for security investments, architecture and infrastructure changes, third-party onboarding and incident response capacity.

• Model uncertainty properly. Use probability distributions, Monte Carlo simulation and loss exceedance curves instead of single-point estimates or ordinal scores. Aggregate risks by simulation, not by adding scores.

• Combine internal incident data, technical security assessment results, industry loss data, threat intelligence and calibrated expert estimates. Update the models with Bayesian methods as new evidence arrives.

• Run cost-benefit analysis and value-of-information analysis on alternative controls, including "do nothing" and "accept the risk and insure it."

• Embed analysis in existing processes. Build risk analysis into change management, architecture review, procurement and budgeting, so it happens inside the decisions people already make. It should not become a separate risk process.

• Make metrics risk-aware. Add uncertainty ranges and leading indicators to existing operational and security KPIs instead of building a standalone KRI catalogue.

• Present findings to senior leadership as decision trade-offs: ranges, probabilities and money.

• Produce regulatory and audit documentation as a by-product of the decision analysis, with minimal extra effort.

• Partner with IT, Information Security, and risk owners to define risk treatment plans, evaluate control effectiveness, and monitor remediation activities

• Collaborate with stakeholders across the organisation to promote consistent risk management practices, strengthen risk ownership, and improve risk awareness

• Strong understanding of probability distributions, Monte Carlo simulation, sensitivity analysis, and basic Bayesian reasoning.

• Practical experience with Python, R, or spreadsheet simulation tools such as SIPmath or ModelRisk.

• Solid understanding of infrastructure, cloud, application security, and attack paths, enabling effective collaboration with engineers and Information Security SMEs.

• Strong quantitative foundation, ideally supported by a degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Economics, or a related field.

• Familiarity with FAIR or a similar approach is a plus, with greater emphasis on mathematical understanding than formal certification.

• Ability to explain complex quantitative concepts, such as loss exceedance curves, clearly and concisely to senior leadership.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex risk assessments into actionable recommendations for technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership.

BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE


Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout,  xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.




THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

We are looking for a Security GRC Lead to own security governance, risk, and compliance across Payward's acquisitions. You will be the accountable owner for bringing each acquired company from its own control environment into ours, working with the M&A Technology Team from diligence through to either full platform migration or steady-state coverage under our central program.

Payward acquires and integrates companies continuously, across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory regimes. Every target arrives with its own controls, its own maturity level and its own audit history, and every one enters our financial statement audit scope on a timeline set by the deal rather than by readiness. Today that work competes for the same people who run controls for the parent company. This role exists so that it has a dedicated owner.

This is a build role to uphold the repeatable process for assessing an acquired company against our security baseline, mapping its controls into our compliance frameworks,and setting remediation milestones a newly acquired team can realistically hit. You will then run it, deal after deal, and you are accountable for the work getting done.

 


THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Assess each acquisition target against Payward's security baseline, during diligence where deal timelines allow and immediately post-close otherwise

 - Map the acquired company's existing controls to Payward's control framework, and identify gaps against the external frameworks the entity falls under once in scope

 - Score control maturity at the entity level and document the basis for each score

 - Define remediation milestones that are achievable for the acquired team's size and maturity, sequenced by risk reduction rather than by framework order

 - Track milestones to closure and report status to Security GRC leadership and the M&A Technology Team

 - Recommend the endpoint for each entity: full migration onto Payward platforms, or uplift to a maturity level the central program can absorb

 - Load acquired-entity risks into the enterprise risk register and keep them current

 - Prepare acquired entities for inclusion in external audit scope, including evidence collection and walkthrough support

 - Act as the Security GRC point of contact for acquired-entity leadership, finance, and internal audit

 - Maintain policy coverage for acquired entities, including building entity-specific policy libraries where the parent policy set does not apply cleanly

 - Feed recurring findings back into the diligence process, so later deals are assessed against known patterns

 - Document the onboarding process so that it is repeatable and not dependent on one person

 


WHAT WILL YOU DO

 - Target Assessment
   
   - Review target security posture during diligence: control environment, identity and access management, infrastructure, third-party dependencies, and prior audit or examination history
   
   - Produce a written assessment of each target against the Payward security baseline, separating the risks that matter to the deal from those that matter to steady-state operations
   
   - Give the M&A Technology Team and deal sponsors a clear read on what integration will cost in control remediation terms

 - Control Mapping and Framework Onboarding
   
   - Map acquired controls to Payward's framework and to the external frameworks the entity becomes subject to
   
   - Identify which parent-company controls extend to the entity as they are, which need an entity-specific variant, and which have no equivalent at all

 - Experimentation and commercial judgment. You design reliable tests, interpret uncertainty honestly, and distinguish attribution from incremental growth. You understand acquisition cost and payback, including downstream retention, revenue, and fully loaded incentive and fraud costs.

Identify and implement optimisation opportunities independently within agreed commercial and compliance guardrails.

Build and maintain prospecting, retargeting and lifecycle audience structures aligned to campaign objectives and customer journey stages.

Use approved first-party, website, app-engagement and platform audiences, including custom audiences, lookalike or equivalent expansion and automated audience products where appropriate.

Turn audience findings into clear actions across targeting, exclusions, budget allocation, creative briefs and campaign structure.

Monitor spend against approved plans by platform, market and campaign, maintaining an accurate pacing view.

Flag over- or underspend risk early, explain the cause and recommend corrective action.

Reallocate budget within agreed guardrails based on performance, delivery opportunity, downstream quality and business priority.

Escalate material budget, tracking, policy or inventory constraints before they affect delivery.

Analyse performance by creative concept, hook, message, proposition, format, duration, placement, call to action and variation where data is available.

Identify winning and underperforming patterns, creative fatigue and gaps in platform-native asset coverage.

Convert findings into clear test hypotheses and prioritised recommendations rather than descriptive commentary.

Brief the creative team on new concepts, iterations and platform-native variations, including objective, audience, insight, hook, message, format, required versions and success metric.

Track assets from briefing through launch and post-test analysis, documenting learning for future iterations and localisation.

Monitor post-click conversion performance using available analytics, segmented by platform, campaign, audience, creative, device, market and landing page where useful.

Identify likely friction, message mismatch, weak journey alignment, broken links, tracking gaps or page-performance issues that may suppress conversion.

Check destination URLs, deep links, app-store routes, UTMs and campaign-to-page alignment as part of launch and ongoing QA.

Interpret results carefully, distinguishing directional evidence from conclusive findings and documenting limitations.

Record outcomes, decisions and next actions so learning can be reused across platforms and markets.

Support conversion-lift, brand-lift and incrementality studies through setup, QA and data collection under the direction of the paid social lead or measurement team.

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout,  xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.




THE TEAM

Payward Services is an enterprise infrastructure platform that enables companies to seamlessly integrate trading, payments, funding, and digital asset services through a single unified system. It provides coordinated liquidity, custody, compliance, risk management, and settlement capabilities, reducing operational complexity for fintechs, banks, brokerages, and payment providers.

As the first dedicated Sales Operations Analyst on the team, you’ll support Business Development across PWS and xStocks so our salespeople can spend their time selling. You’ll run RFP and DDQ responses from start to finish, prepare the team for diligence meetings, qualify and route inbound leads, and keep our CRM, pipeline reporting, and customer insights accurate. You’ll report to PWS sales leadership and work closely with Business Operations, Solutions, Legal, Compliance, and Product.

 


THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own RFP and DDQ responses for PWS and xStocks from kickoff through submission: triage incoming questions, route technical and compliance items to Solutions and Compliance, and make sure answers are validated before they go out

 - Coordinate contributions from Legal, Compliance, Security, Product, Engineering, and other internal teams, establishing deadlines and driving follow-up to ensure timely, complete responses

 - Oversee document assembly and final formatting to ensure every submission is accurate, polished, and delivered on schedule

 - Lead internal preparation and alignment for major client presentations, particularly RFP due diligence meetings, and track action items through to resolution

 - Qualify inbound leads, including follow-up qualifying questions where needed, and route them promptly to the right salesperson or to self-serve onboarding

 - Maintain Attio CRM data integrity, ensuring accounts, contacts, deal stages, and client outreach activity are accurate and consistent with Salesforce and other teams’ systems

 - Build and maintain pipeline reporting in Attio, including stage definitions, funnel metrics, and forecast inputs, and prepare materials for weekly pipeline reviews

 - Manage the handoff from signed deal to onboarding, confirming contracts, pricing, and billing details are in place so Solutions and Finance can start without chasing information

 - Produce weekly customer insights from call notes and CRM activity, summarizing product requests, competitor feedback, and pricing feedback, and communicate emerging trends to Sales, Product, and leadership

 - Develop and maintain a library of approved RFP and DDQ responses, and use it with AI tools to draft accurate, consistent first-pass answers

 - Identify process gaps and implement better workflows, automating repetitive work where possible

 - Perform additional duties and responsibilities as assigned

 


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 3+ years of experience in sales operations, sales support, or proposal management, ideally within banking, fintech, financial services, or crypto

 - Experience managing RFPs, DDQs, security or compliance questionnaires, or other complex documents with many contributors

 - Proven ability to drive deadlines and coordinate cross-functional stakeholders across Legal, Compliance, Security, Product, and other teams

 - Hands-on experience with a CRM platform (Attio experience is a plus; Salesforce or HubSpot experience is transferable)

 - Comfort building simple reports and dashboards

 - Excellent writing, editing, and document formatting skills

 - Clear, confident communication with senior internal stakeholders and external clients

 - Understanding of institutional and B2B sales cycles in financial services

 - Interest in crypto and digital assets (prior industry experience is not required)

 - Proactive, process-oriented approach, with the ability to identify issues and implement effective solutions

 - Rigorous attention to detail

 


NICE TO HAVES

 - Background in banking, institutional sales, or B2B infrastructure and API products

 - Familiarity with vendor due diligence and security questionnaires

 - Experience using AI tools or workflow automation to speed up repetitive sales or operations work

Kraken’s Core Infrastructure Engineering team builds and operates the shared data systems behind critical production services. Our estate spans on-premises and cloud infrastructure, with MariaDB at its centre and Kafka, Redis and Elasticsearch across the wider platform.

We’re hiring a Principal Database Engineer to bring long-term experience and technical judgment to this estate. You’ll assess it, set the goals and direction, and work hands-on with the team to deliver measurable improvements. This is an individual contributor role with influence across teams and several quarters of work.

 


THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Review the estate against business needs and production evidence. Judge reliability, scale, cost and operational complexity, identifying what should be preserved and where investment or simplification would make a difference.

 - Define the target architecture and measurable goals. Agree a prioritised roadmap with engineering leads and dependent teams, explaining the trade-offs and sequencing work around delivery risks.

 - Execute that roadmap with the team through design, implementation and adoption. Stay personally involved in difficult migrations and scaling decisions, with representative benchmarks, data-integrity checks and credible cutover and rollback plans. Adapt the plan as evidence changes and verify the results in production before calling the work complete.

 - Investigate difficult MariaDB failures and performance limits through the engine, storage and application behaviour. Improve fleet reliability through useful observability, safer changes and tested backup, restore and disaster recovery procedures. Set recovery objectives with service owners and prove them through exercises.

 - Build and maintain production software for database provisioning, upgrades and routine maintenance. Make self-service workflows safe and auditable, incorporating access controls and change evidence with Security and Compliance.

 - Work with application teams on schemas, transaction boundaries, queries and data-store choices. Make the operational consequences clear and resolve dependencies that span teams.

 - Mentor engineers across the team through design reviews, pairing and incident analysis. Help them deepen their database expertise and take ownership of technical decisions.

 - Participate in on-call and incident response, leaving clear operational ownership and following through on lessons from production.

 


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 8+ years operating and evolving production database estates at scale. You have assessed inherited systems, set technical direction and delivered improvements with engineering teams, and can explain how those decisions held up over time.

 - Strong understanding of high availability, replication and distributed database failure modes. You can explain consistency and availability trade-offs and reason about transaction boundaries and reliable event delivery, including transactional outbox patterns.

 - Deep, recent hands-on MariaDB expertise, including InnoDB, MVCC and transaction isolation, locking, query optimisation, binary logs and MariaDB GTID replication. You can explain the mechanisms and diagnostic evidence behind your decisions.

 - Personal ownership of MariaDB incident diagnosis, performance tuning and tested restore or point-in-time recovery. You can explain what you did, how you established data integrity and what remained uncertain.

 - Strong software engineering skills in Python, Go, Rust or a comparable language. You have personally built and maintained production software or automation for database workflows such as provisioning, failover, online schema changes and self-service operations, using version control, code review and delivery pipelines, with tested failure handling.

 - Strong low-level Linux, Kernel, storage and networking fundamentals, with the ability to investigate problems beyond the database process.

 - Clear written technical judgment and demonstrated delivery across teams without reporting-line authority. You help stakeholders make sound database design and lifecycle decisions, and develop experienced engineers through shared delivery.

 


NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience operating databases in containerised, hybrid on-premises/cloud or multi-region environments. Familiarity with Kubernetes, infrastructure as code or GitOps, including their operational trade-offs.

 - Experience with database proxies or load-balancing layers (MaxScale, HAProxy, ProxySQL, or similar).

 - Experience with PostgreSQL, Vitess, TiDB, ScyllaDB, ClickHouse or internal database platforms; operational knowledge of Kafka, Redis/Valkey or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch.

 - Experience in regulated environments or contributions to database engines, operators and other infrastructure software.

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout,  xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.




THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

As Director, US Operations, you will lead operations for Payward’s US equities business: our registered broker-dealer, Kraken Securities LLC, and the operations behind traditional stocks as well as xStocks, our tokenized equities product. You will own the trade operating model, the end-to-end order and settlement flow, cash flows, corporate actions, reconciliations, and regulatory readiness across the business.

This is a hands-on leadership role in a regulated entity. You will be a registered principal of Kraken Securities LLC, named on Form BD, and accountable for the operational side of the firm’s regulatory obligations. It extends well beyond day-to-day management and requires genuine fluency in both traditional market plumbing and the operational realities of a digital-asset business.

You will stay close to company strategy and cross-functional initiatives so the global executive team’s goals translate into clear operating priorities. As a trusted partner, you will work across Compliance, Legal, Finance, Product, Engineering, and Marketing to drive key initiatives forward, and build the team that scales the business as the firm grows.

The opportunity

 - Own the end-to-end US equities order flow, from inception through clearing and settlement, including reconciliation, corporate actions, and exception management.

 - Own xStocks operations, including token issuance and redemption, inventory and liquidity management, movement of client and firm assets, and settlement across exchange, custodian, and on-chain venues.

 - Serve as a named principal of Kraken Securities LLC and as an operational control point, providing dual-approval (“four eyes”) sign-off on transactions and asset movements, with coverage across time zones.

 - Design and implement the operating model for Kraken Securities and xStocks, aligned to strategic goals, and contribute to strategy and growth planning to help build a sustainable business.

 - Build and run the operating systems for the business (policies, written supervisory procedures, controls, books and records, and business continuity), translating C-suite goals into clear targets for each business unit, then setting performance targets, tracking progress, and reporting KPIs and costs transparently to leadership.

 - Own launch readiness for new products and markets by preparing systems, policies, and procedures, and testing them end to end with clearing, custody, exchange, and R&D partners to ensure US regulatory compliance.

 - Ensure desk coverage, settlement and reconciliation controls, and staffing are in place to support 24x5 and the transition to 24x7, and own severity-1 escalation and incident response for the US entities, including root-cause review and remediation.

 - Partner with Finance on controls around bank payments, customer funds, and reserve requirements, and own vendor and partner operations (clearing, custody, market data, liquidity providers, and technology), including onboarding, SLAs, and ongoing oversight.

 - Hire and develop a high-performing operations team, build the licensing bench and succession plan, and design the organizational structure to scale.

 - Partner with Marketing, Compliance, Product, Engineering, and Operations to keep initiatives aligned and moving, and support HR and IT in building procedures that link to corporate strategy.

What you bring

 - 12+ years in brokerage, fintech, or operations consulting, including time inside a FINRA-registered broker-dealer, and experience in crypto, brokerage, advisory, fintech, or another highly regulated industry.

 - In-depth knowledge of traditional markets: execution, clearing, settlement, custody, margin, securities lending, and corporate actions.

 - Working understanding of digital assets and tokenized securities, including custody models, on-chain settlement, and the controls they demand.

 - Direct experience under SEC and FINRA rules: books and records, supervisory procedures, trade reporting, and examination response.

 - Experience standing up or scaling operations for a new regulated product or entity, including launch readiness and regulatory approvals.

 - A proven record of defining structured approaches to complex challenges, with end-to-end understanding of company value drivers and strong business analytics.

 - Experience hiring, managing, and developing operations teams.

 - Exceptional judgment and the executive presence to work with C-suite leaders, regulators, and external partners.

Licenses and eligibility

 - Required at hire, or within an agreed window from start date: FINRA Series 7 (General Securities Representative), Series 99 (Operations Professional) and Series 24 (General Securities Principal)

 - Preferred: Series 27 or 28 (Financial and Operations Principal)

 - Also valued: Series 57 (Securities Trader) and Series 4  (options principal), or willingness to obtain them — these strengthen our principal coverage across trading and options

We are seeking a senior trust, custody, and treasury professional to serve as Chief Trust Officer and Treasurer for an OCC-chartered trust bank and a state-chartered trust bank. This role combines responsibility for the safety and control of client assets with oversight of the bank’s treasury operations, balance sheet, capital, and liquidity.
The successful candidate will bring deep experience in digital-asset custody and treasury operations, sound judgment in regulated environments, and the ability to operate effectively in a growing, cross-functional organization.

• Serve as Trust Officer and Treasurer, subject to applicable regulatory approval and required vetting.

• Oversee fund movements, ensuring appropriate controls, documentation, and approvals.

• Oversee account reconciliations and help ensure client assets are safeguarded, accurately recorded, and supported by strong financial controls.

• Oversee bank accounts and treasury operations, including management of the balance sheet and capital and liquidity buffers.

• Partner with Legal, Compliance, Finance, Operations, Product, and senior leadership on regulatory expectations, controls, and operating readiness.

• Support the design, implementation, and ongoing improvement of custody, treasury, reconciliation, and financial-control processes.

• Prepare for and support financial-statement, custody, SOC, and other applicable audits and regulatory reviews.

• At least 10 years of relevant professional experience in digital-asset custody, treasury operations, banking, trust, or closely related fields.

• Demonstrated experience with digital-asset custody and treasury operations; experience at a crypto custodian, regulated trust company, or bank is strongly valued.

• Experience working with the OCC or a state banking regulator, or directly supporting a regulated trust or banking organization through regulatory requirements.

• Strong understanding of bank accounts, balance-sheet management, capital, liquidity, reconciliations, and financial controls.

• Ability to be based in Chicago and work from the Chicago office as needed in a hybrid environment.

• Ability to pass required government background checks relating to financial condition and character.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience working for or with a digital-asset custodian.

• Experience with custody of traditional assets, combined with a demonstrated willingness and ability to develop deep expertise in crypto custody.

• Experience supporting financial-statement audits, custody audits, SOC audits, or similar control assessments.

• Design, build, and deliver IAM engineering solutions including IGA, IdP/SSO, PAM, and directory services implementations.

• Develop target-state identity architectures and integration patterns that support cohesive joiner-mover-leaver lifecycle processes, secure access, data quality, and operational scalability.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world’s longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. We’re looking for a Full Stack Engineer to join a small, dedicated growth and experimentation team within Krak, focused on accelerating acquisition, activation, engagement and trading activity across the Krak app. This is a frontend-leaning full-stack role: the majority of your work will be in React Native, supported by enough backend capability to take an experiment from idea to live without waiting on another team.

 

Rather than executing against a rigid roadmap, you’ll work closely with Product on a continuous pipeline of fast, lightweight experiments, owning each one from hypothesis through implementation, launch, measurement and iteration. The mandate is simple: find the highest-leverage opportunities to grow users and revenue, prove what works, and scale the winners – with direct, measurable impact on how millions of customers discover and use Kraken’s products.

 

The opportunity

 - Build and ship consumer-facing features quickly in React Native and TypeScript, favouring small, high-velocity experiments over long-running projects.

 - Own experiments end-to-end – hypothesis, design, build, launch, measurement and iteration – using platforms such as Statsig to test globally or within specific markets.

 - Improve onboarding, activation and feature discovery to drive conversion, engagement and trading revenue, iterating rapidly on features that are already live.

 - Build viral acquisition features and value-add growth features on top of Krak’s existing product offering.

 - Contribute to backend services and APIs wherever an experiment requires it, so you can ship across the stack without being blocked. Our backend is primarily Rust; prior Rust experience is not expected, but enthusiasm for picking it up is.

 - Read your own results, including trade-offs between conversion gains and other metrics, and decide whether to scale, iterate or kill – driving technical decisions autonomously amid evolving priorities and limited upfront planning.

 

What you bring

 - 3+ years of software development experience building and shipping large-scale, consumer-facing applications. Strong, hands-on React and React Native experience is essential.

 - Demonstrated experience running growth experiments at consumer-facing businesses, with measurable impact on conversion, activation, retention or revenue. This is a consumer growth role, so B2B or platform-only backgrounds are not a fit.

 - Working backend proficiency: you can design and implement services and APIs yourself. We care about backend fundamentals rather than any particular language, and you should be open to working in Rust.

 - Strong JavaScript/TypeScript fundamentals, with hands-on experience across APIs, WebSockets and real-time systems, mobile performance, testing, and modern development workflows.

 - Practical experience designing, running and analysing A/B tests – feature flags, statistical significance, product analytics, funnel and cohort data – with the judgement to act decisively on what the results show.

 - End-to-end ownership of product features and a strong product engineering mindset, with the initiative and adaptability to operate with minimal direction amid ambiguity and frequently changing priorities.

 

Nice to haves

 - Customer-facing product experience within fintech, digital banking, payments, trading or crypto.

 - Hands-on experience with Statsig or a comparable experimentation platform, including regional and global rollouts.

 - Rust experience, given our backend stack.

 - SQL and self-serve analytics, so you can pull and interrogate your own data.

 - AI fluency. Familiarity with how AI tools and patterns have fundamentally shifted your development workflow and problem-solving approach.

 - Native mobile development (iOS/Android), distributed systems or microservices, or engineering within a hyperscaling consumer technology organisation.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About the Team

OKX Internal Audit is the organization's independent third line of defense, reporting to the Board and the Group Audit and Risk Committee on the design and effectiveness of governance, risk management, and internal controls across a global, multi-entity crypto exchange. The function executes a risk-based annual audit plan covering financial, operational, technology, security, and regulatory risk, and operates with full, unrestricted access to systems, records, and personnel.

Within Internal Audit, the Platform & Infrastructure team sits inside the Global Platform & Engineering (GP&E) team and owns assurance over the technology foundation that keeps the exchange running: network administration, cloud infrastructure and infrastructure-as-code, containerization and orchestration, middleware services, site reliability and disaster recovery, and the data pipelines feeding OKX's financial and operational systems. Reflecting a multi-cloud environment (AWS, Alibaba Cloud, GCP) supporting live trading, custody, and customer-facing operations on a global scale.

About the Role

As Senior Manager, Platform & Infrastructure Audit, you'll be a hands-on, deeply technical individual-contributor auditor who owns critical assurance projects spanning the cloud infrastructure and DevOps lifecycle, from platform build and configuration through CI/CD pipelines and hands-on ITGC validation. You'll bring subject matter expertise to both dimensions of AI in scope: auditing AI (assessing how OKX's AI/ML systems are built, governed, and monitored) and auditing with AI (applying AI tools to your own scoping, testing, and reporting) while also flexing into adjacent domains such as cloud security and identity, resilience engineering, secure SDLC, and data engineering. You'll help shape the risk-based audit plan by identifying emerging infrastructure risks, and partner closely with Engineering, SRE, and Security stakeholders to deliver findings and recommendations that hold up in a fast-moving, high-technology crypto environment.

What You'll be Doing

•

Cloud Infrastructure & Platform Engineering Audit (SME): Deep, hands-on expertise auditing cloud platforms (Alibaba Cloud, AWS), containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes), CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm).

•

AI Use, Adoption & Governance: Two dimensions, both required.

•

Auditing AI: Assessing how AI/ML systems are built, deployed, and monitored — model and data lineage, training-data provenance and quality, access to models and prompts, human-in-the-loop and approval controls, evaluation and drift monitoring, and alignment to emerging AI governance and regulatory expectations.

•

Auditing with AI: A demonstrated bias toward using AI in your own audit work — scoping, evidence review, control testing, script generation, and reporting — and an interest in helping the function build reusable AI-enabled audit tooling.

What We Look For in You

•

Crypto & Blockchain Acumen: Prior experience at a crypto exchange or with a crypto product is preferred.

•

Critical Thinking for Complex Environments: A proven capacity to analyze novel technical and control environments unique to crypto, identify intricate root causes, and propose effective, context-specific remediation that engineering teams will actually adopt.

•

Breadth Across Adjacent Platform Domains: Demonstrable experience auditing control design and operating effectiveness in several of the following:

•

Cloud security and identity — IAM, network segmentation, secrets management, encryption and key management

•

Site reliability and resilience — observability, incident and problem management, capacity, backup and disaster recovery

•

Software development lifecycle — code review, branch protection, artifact integrity, secure SDLC, third-party and open-source dependency risk

•

Data engineering and analytics — integrity and quality of data pipelines and ETL processes

•

AI/ML platform and MLOps — model registries, feature stores, inference infrastructure, and the data feeding them

Nice to Haves

•

Cloud or Security Certifications: AWS or GCP professional-level certification, Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA), CISA, CISSP, or CCSK/CCSP.

•

Crypto and blockchain literacy: regulated financial-services, fintech, or crypto experience.

•

Mandarin speaking

Perks & Benefits

•

Competitive total compensation package

•

L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development

•

Various team building programs and company events

•

Wellness and meal allowances

•

Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

•

More that we love to tell you along the process!

OKX Statement:

OKX is committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, genetic information, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, lawful alien status, national origin, age, marital status, and non-job related physical or mental disability, or protected veteran status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

•

The salary range for this position is $171,000 - $257,000

•

The salary offered depends on a variety of factors, including job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and market location. In addition to the salary, a performance bonus and long-term incentives may be provided as part of the compensation package, as well as a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the position offered. Applicants should apply via OKX internal or external careers site.

Notice:

All official OKX vacancies are published on this website. While roles may appear on selected third-party platforms from time to time, information on other sites may be inaccurate or outdated. If in doubt, please apply directly through our official careers website.

Information collected and processed as part of the recruitment process of any job application you choose to submit is subject to OKX's Candidate Privacy Notice.

•

Own day-to-day entity maintenance across multiple regulated entities in Switzerland and the EU: domiciliation, annual filings, commercial register updates, corporate registers and routine corporate secretarial actions.

Prepare and manage KYB and KYC documentation packs for banks, crypto exchanges and commercial partners, and keep them up to date.

Run contract management: intake, signature, archiving, versioning and tracking of renewals and key deadlines.

Support the Legal team with signature workflows and board and shareholder documentation.

Handle incoming legal and administrative requests in coordination with Legal and Compliance.

•

Handle incoming and outgoing corporate mail, registered letters and couriers for group entities.

Handle highly confidential documentation (UBO declarations, identity documents, banking records, officer sign-off documents) with strict data privacy and security controls.

Use and improve AI-powered tools and automations to streamline filings, KYB packs, contract tracking and reporting.

Run small pilots, measure results, and scale what works.

We are hiring a Senior Database Reliability Engineer for our Infrastructure Platform Team. You will design PostgreSQL platforms for resilience and high availability, automate everything you touch, and understand how our services use the database, from connection pools to ORM transactions. Your goal is to keep latency within SLO at a reasonable cost, through every change, failover and migration.
Our stack today: AWS RDS and Aurora (PostgreSQL, MySQL), Redshift, ClickHouse, Terraform, Ansible, Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics and Grafana, with Java services on Kubernetes.


Responsibilities:
• Design and run highly available PostgreSQL across zones and regions, with automated, tested failover and fencing against split-brain.

• Define all database infrastructure as code (clusters, parameters, networking, access, monitoring and backups), reviewed by peers and applied through CI/CD pipelines, with drift detection.

• Build self-service database provisioning so product teams get a production-ready database without waiting on a ticket.Plan and execute migrations, upgrades and table moves with zero or near zero downtime, including cross-version, cross-cluster and cross-cloud work.

• Partner with developers on schema changes, queries, connection pooling, transaction scope, retries and expand-and-contract migrations, so database issues are fixed at their source.

• Define SLOs and build SLO-based alerts and dashboards (Prometheus, Grafana or similar) that catch latency and capacity problems before clients do.

• Design backup and recovery, and prove it with scheduled restore and failover tests that measure RTO and RPO and produce evidence for auditors.

• Keep cost in view: right-size instances and storage, and choose the cheapest option that meets the requirement.

• Secure the data: least-privilege access, secrets from a secrets manager, encryption at rest and in transit, audited access and PII masking.

• Lead and take part in incident response and on-call, write blameless post-mortems and make sure their actions get done.

• Replace manual runbooks with automation, and document what remains.

• 5+ years running production databases as a DBRE, SRE, platform or database engineer, ideally with a large part on AWS (RDS or Aurora).

• Experience designing high availability and disaster recovery: replication, automated failover, multi-region or multi-cloud redundancy, and the trade-offs between RTO, RPO and cost.

• A track record of zero-downtime changes: online migrations, major version upgrades or moving data between clusters.

• Understanding of how applications use databases: connection pools, ORMs (for example Hibernate), transaction scope, retries and idempotency, and safe deployment order.

• Observability skills: you define what to measure, alert on SLOs and verify changes with data.Scripting in Python, Bash or Go to automate operational work.

• Clear communication: you reason out loud, own outcomes and partner with developers instead of gatekeeping.

Who we are

We simplify wealth creation. Founded in 2014 in Vienna, Austria by Eric Demuth, Paul Klanschek and Christian Trummer, we’re here to help people trust themselves enough to build their financial freedom — for now and the future. Our user-friendly, trade-everything platform empowers both first-time investors and seasoned experts to invest in the cryptocurrencies, crypto indices, stocks*, precious metals and commodities* they want — with any sized budget, 24/7. Our global team works across different cultures and time zones, bringing our products to more than 7 million customers, making us one of Europe’s safest and most secure platforms that powers modern investing.

Headquartered in Austria but operating across Europe, our products are built by fast-moving, talented, “roll-up-your-sleeves-and-make-it-happen” kind of people. It’s these diverse perspectives and innovative minds operating as ONE TEAM that keep Bitpanda at the cutting edge of our industry. So if you’re someone who thinks big, moves fast and wants to make an impact right from day one, then get ready to join our industry-changing team. Let’s go!

Your mission

Own Bitpanda’s CRM campaigns from brief to result across email, push, in-app banners and stories. You will turn retention, monetisation and lifecycle plans into live, multi-market journeys in Braze, run the campaign calendar across the teams that brief us, and make sure every send is built right, approved and measured. You join a small central CRM team that is becoming the engine behind how we talk to our customers. This role will either be hired in Vienna (AT), Barcelona (ES) or Krakow (PL).

What you'll do

• Build and launch campaigns in Braze across email, push, in-app banners and stories: segmentation, canvases, templates, personalisation and testing.

• Own the channel mix for every campaign, choosing the right channel, sequence and frequency for each audience and using test results to keep refining it.

• Run the campaign calendar across markets with Growth Operations and the regional market leads.

• Coordinate copy, localisation and compliance approvals so campaigns ship on time and correctly.

• Own QA before every send and report on performance against our shared Growth KPIs afterwards, turning results and learnings into improvements to the lifecycle strategy.

Who you are

• You built campaigns in Braze (or similar CRM tool) yourself and have done so in your most recent role; you know canvases, segments and Liquid.

• You know from data and experience which channel works best for which audience and moment, and how to orchestrate email, push and in-app messaging so they reinforce rather than compete with each other.

• You have run multi-market campaigns end to end, including QA and reporting, ideally in fintech, iGaming or e-commerce, and can show a result you were accountable for and explain what you would do differently.

• You have experience working in an environment where communications require compliance approval and know how to factor that into your planning.

• You are highly organised and can keep track of requests from several teams at once without letting anything slip through.

What’s in it for you

• Flexibility to work where you thrive – Enjoy the freedom of our Hybrid working model, combining onsite collaboration and remote work, with an additional 25 days per year to work from a city or country of your choice.

• Reward for your impact – Receive a competitive total compensation package aligned with Bitpanda’s pay-for-impact policy, including participation in our stock option plan.

• Support for your mental wellbeing – Access confidential coaching, counselling, and mental health resources whenever you need them through OpenUP.

• Time to recharge – On top of your standard annual leave, prioritise your wellbeing in 2027 with 3 additional days of paid time off to rest, reset, and recharge, available once you’ve been with us for 6 months.

• Continuous learning and growth – Grow your skills and stay ahead in your career with unlimited access to Udemy’s library of online courses at your own pace.

• Exclusive perks and rewards – Enjoy discounts, rewards, and perks from partners worldwide across lifestyle, wellness, tech, and travel.

• Support during life milestones – Take advantage of up to 8 additional weeks of gender-neutral new parent leave to welcome and bond with your new addition to the family.

• Fuel and focus on-site – Pandas in Vienna, Bucharest, Barcelona, and Berlin can enjoy free onsite dining, with freshly prepared lunches and snacks to keep you fueled and focused all day long.

• Recognition for your contributions – Celebrate milestones and achievements with recognition and rewards for your Tenure at Bitpanda.

• Show your Bitpanda pride – Access exclusive Bitpanda-branded merchandise and gear to represent.

• Connect and celebrate with your team – Join unforgettable company events, from our Winter Party in Vienna to gatherings worldwide, fostering fun, connection, and celebration

.…and even more location-specific benefits designed to make life at Bitpanda even more rewarding wherever you are.

Above all, you will have the opportunity to learn and grow as part of Bitpanda’s incredible journey towards being Europe’s future #1 investment platform.

Bitpanda is committed to fostering a fair and equal environment based on trust and mutual respect. We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace is paramount to our success and we are committed to building a team that represents a wide variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.

• Shape what customers see, sign, and own in the Bitpanda app, including how liquidation and risk are explained, and measure real use: borrowers who come back, bad debt and revenue, not total value locked alone.

• Recommend which protocols and partners come to Vision Chain, backed by a business case, and work with Legal, Compliance and Risk from day one on EU consumer credit rules and MiCA.

Who you are

• 6+ years of Product Management experience, with at least 3+ years focused specifically on building and scaling DeFi or crypto products.

• You know lending markets in depth: collateral and liquidation mechanics, interest rate models, oracles and how they fail, curation and bad debt. You're at home with the EVM and can read Solidity smart contract code well enough to question engineers about it.

• Demonstrated experience bringing DeFi applications into regulated consumer products and successfully bridging the gap between decentralized and centralized finance.

• Ability to lead through influence, build clear business cases, and write excellent documentation in English. This includes a strong working knowledge of EU crypto regulations (e.g., MiCA) to effectively partner with Risk, Legal, and Compliance teams.

• Nice to haves:

• hands-on experience scaling onchain ecosystem liquidity from scratch

• knowledge of and/or work experience in traditional financial markets

** This position is available in all of our Hubs.
